title: P2 — /api/v1/dashboard win totals mix populations per side and hardcode CANCELLED 0: serves 88 mafia + 916 town = 1004 wins beside its own completed 4402 (town under-reported by 3398), statusBreakdown sums to 4403 against totals.total 5092

detail.text: Dogfood 2026-11-20, live :3004, capability under test 2b780d3 (main advanced to 5657e0d during the tick). Real user path: open the dashboard tab. curl /api/v1/dashboard returns totals.total=5092, totals.active=1, totals.completed=4402 and wins={mafia:88,town:916}. 88+916=1004, i.e. 3398 town wins are missing from the very tile that shows completed=4402. The same corpus on /api/v1/stats is self-consistent: mafiaWins 88 + townWins 4314 = 4402 completed. Cause (read, not guessed): apps/server/src/routes/stats.ts:74 takes the mafia side as `aggregatedWins.mafiaWins || gameStats.mafiaWins` — the aggregated sample returned 0 mafia wins, 0 is falsy, so the || silently substituted the full-population column count (88); the town side has no fallback because its sample value (916) is truthy, so the two halves of one pie come from two different populations. Sample source: apps/server/src/services/stats-collector/wins.ts:41-52 does listGames({status:'ENDED',limit:1000}) then one events query per game. Reproduced independently on a copy of the 14:23 dump with .coding-hermes/evidence/2026-11-20-dogfood-141933/n1_probe.py: newest 1000 ENDED games yield mafia=0 town=1000 (recent corpus is mock/canned TOWN games), confirming the sample is both biased and partial. Second defect in the same payload: statusBreakdown is served as {completed:4402,inProgress:1,cancelled:0} while SELECT status,count(*) FROM games GROUP BY status returns CANCELLED 206 / ENDED 4885 / IN_PROGRESS 1, so 206 cancelled games are invisible and the breakdown sums to 4403, not 5092. Supersedes nothing: DF-41 (report summary divides mock-excluded wins by mock-inclusive completed) and DF-41-R2 (/benchmark/report/summary does not declare its population) are the same class on other surfaces and are both complete; this row is the dashboard surface, still live. Fix: compute both sides from one population in one query, drop the || fallback idiom for explicit null checks, and derive statusBreakdown with GROUP BY instead of the hardcoded literal.

acceptance_criteria: PASS: `(cd apps/server && pnpm test:run)` exits 0; on a warm server `curl -s localhost:3004/api/v1/dashboard | jq -r '.data | ((.wins.mafia + .wins.town) - .totals.completed)'` prints 0; `curl -s localhost:3004/api/v1/dashboard | jq -r '.data.statusBreakdown.cancelled'` equals `docker exec mafia-ai-benchmark-server-1 node -e "console.log(require('/app/apps/server/node_modules/better-sqlite3')('/app/data/mafia.db',{readonly:true}).prepare(\"SELECT count(*) c FROM games WHERE status='CANCELLED'\").get().c)"`; and no `|| gameStats.` fallback remains on the win fields in apps/server/src/routes/stats.ts.
acceptance: PASS: dashboard wins sum to totals.completed (jq difference prints 0); statusBreakdown.cancelled equals the DB CANCELLED count (206 at time of filing); pnpm test:run green.

title: P2 — every mafia_game_* Prometheus metric serves 0 on the live deployment: mafia_game_ended_total{outcome=*} all 0 beside 4885 ENDED games, so the wired fleet scrape and its two alerts can only ever fire on zeros

detail.text: Dogfood 2026-11-20, live :3004 (uptime-fresh container; capability under test 2b780d3, main advanced to 5657e0d during the tick). curl /metrics returns 1511 non-comment lines; filtering out lines ending in 0 leaves exactly 8 samples and all 8 are process_* (process_cpu_user_seconds_total 25.251895, process_resident_memory_bytes 118845440, ...). Every product metric is zero: mafia_game_active 0, mafia_game_ended_total{outcome="completed"} 0, {outcome="cancelled"} 0, {outcome="failed"} 0, {outcome="degenerate"} 0 — while the same deployment's DB holds games=5092 with 4885 ENDED and 206 CANCELLED and its own /api/v1/stats reports completedGames 4402. The instruments are registered (they appear with labels and HELP/TYPE) but never incremented on the path this deployment actually runs — the games are produced through the legacy adapter, so nothing reaches the counters. This is a live-vs-claimed gap, not a duplicate: docs/api-reference.md:100-121 documents GET /metrics as the enforced Tier-0 surface, docs/observability-spec.md:15 maps OBS-001 to commit d1a109b, and OBS-001 (5 Tier-0 game metrics) / OBS-003 (orphan gauge) / OBS-006 (make mafia_game_in_progress honest) / OBS-004 (wire the fleet-monitor scrape job + 2 alert rules) are all marked complete — so fleet-monitor is scraping a product that reports zero activity, and any spawn-failure or no-games alert is blind. Confirms the same defect class as the OBS-006 intent: the gauge is not lying in isolation, no game path emits anything at all. Fix: emit the counters from the single place a game reaches a terminal status (the legacy adapter's end-of-game handler), and add a smoke assertion that a completed game increments mafia_game_ended_total. Observed registry: apps/server/src/observability/metrics.ts.

acceptance_criteria: PASS: `(cd apps/server && pnpm test:run)` exits 0; after one game reaches a terminal status on a live instance, `curl -s localhost:3004/metrics | grep -E '^mafia_game_ended_total'` prints a non-zero sample whose label matches that game outcome, `curl -s localhost:3004/metrics | grep -E '^mafia_game_active'` tracks the games table IN_PROGRESS count, and a new test asserts the counter increments on game completion.

title: [perf] P3 — /api/v1/dashboard costs 1.52-1.95s on EVERY request with no memoization, and 706ms of it is a measured 1000-game N+1 loop; /api/v1/stats costs 0.70s warm / 1.42s cold for a 9-query payload whose sibling /api/v1/games?limit=50 answers in 8ms

detail.text: Dogfood 2026-11-20, live :3004, 5092 games. Warm reps of the page a user actually opens: /api/v1/dashboard 1.52s / 1.57s / 1.95s (three consecutive curls, nothing cold in the set — the route caches nothing); /api/v1/analytics and /api/v1/stats/models sampled in the same pass. For contrast in the same process: /api/v1/games?limit=50 = 0.008s, /api/v1/benchmark/compare = warm 0.21-0.28s because PERF-MAFIA-3 watermark-memoized it, while /api/v1/stats = 0.70s warm / 1.42s cold. Profile evidence, READ NUMERICALLY rather than eyeballed: the dashboard calls getAggregatedWins, which lists 1000 ENDED games and then issues one events query per game (apps/server/src/services/stats-collector/wins.ts:41-52). Measured that loop exactly on a copy of the 14:23 dump with .coding-hermes/evidence/2026-11-20-dogfood-141933/n1_probe.py: listGames(1000) 104.0ms + 1000 per-game GAME_OVER lookups at 0.706ms each = 706.0ms for the loop alone, i.e. roughly 40-46 percent of the 1.5-2.0s dashboard budget is that N+1, paid on every request. Client caveat stated honestly: the probe uses python3 stdlib sqlite3 against a read-only copy of the dump (node better-sqlite3 was unavailable without writing a file into the live container), so absolute milliseconds differ by driver while the shape and ratio hold; the live curl times above are the server's own numbers. Second cost centre: /api/v1/stats runs 9 statements per request via getGameStats (apps/server/src/db/repository.ts:860) including the DEGENERATE_GAME_SQL / MOCK_GAME_SQL CASE filters (repository.ts:66-120) that scan events with json_extract over the whole corpus, plus a reconcile pass — that is the 0.70s. Accepted as user-noticeable: 1.5-2.0s on every dashboard load is felt; 8ms and 0.28s are not worth a row and none was filed for them. Fix: replace the per-game loop with the single window query already present for getWinnerEventCounts (one pass, GROUP BY game_id) or memoize both endpoints on the same watermark fingerprint PERF-MAFIA-2/3 use.

acceptance_criteria: PASS: `(cd apps/server && pnpm test:run)` exits 0; after a warm-up request on a 4K+ game corpus, `for i in 1 2 3; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{time_total}\n' localhost:3004/api/v1/dashboard; done` prints three values below 0.300 and `for i in 1 2 3; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{time_total}\n' localhost:3004/api/v1/stats; done` prints three values below 0.300; and `grep -rn 'for (const game of' apps/server/src/services/stats-collector/wins.ts` no longer shows a per-game query loop feeding the dashboard.

title: P3 — the Stage-2 restore rehearsal in docs/ops/db-backup-restore.md hardcodes one timestamped dump filename, so the documented cp fails for any operator once retention prunes it (I had to substitute the current dump to run the recipe)

detail.text: Dogfood 2026-11-20: walked the operator backup/restore doc as a copy-paste user. Section 2 sample output (docs/ops/db-backup-restore.md:50) prints file=/mnt/bulk/hermes-backups/mafia-db/mafia-20261120-085632.db, and the Stage-2 rehearsal (section 6, line 246 onward) copies that same literal name: cp /backup/mafia-20261120-085632.db /data/mafia.db. Section 3 states only the newest 14 dumps are kept (MAFIA_DB_BACKUP_RETAIN, line 154), and backups run on a schedule with prune enabled — so within 14 backups (same day at cron cadence) the literal path the doc tells you to copy no longer exists and the recipe dies at cp: cannot stat, which is exactly the moment an operator is under pressure and least able to improvise. Observed friction: to run Stage 2 at 14:23 today I had to substitute mafia-20261120-142323.db for the documented name; the rest of the recipe (docker volume create, the --entrypoint sh copy, the throwaway container, /health, section 6 step 4 teardown) worked as written. Everything else about the path checked out — backup 7.9s, scripts/restore-drill.sh 1.16s, restored counts matched live, teardown step present in the doc. So this is the one rough edge in an otherwise correct doc. Fix: use a placeholder or derive it, e.g. DUMP=$(ls -t /mnt/bulk/hermes-backups/mafia-db/*.db | head -1), and label the section-2 line as sample output rather than a command.

acceptance_criteria: PASS: no literal mafia-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.db path appears in any executable command block of docs/ops/db-backup-restore.md (`grep -nE 'cp .*mafia-2026[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{6}\.db' docs/ops/db-backup-restore.md` returns nothing), the Stage-2 recipe derives the newest dump or takes a DUMP variable, and following the documented commands verbatim against the current backup directory completes the rehearsal including teardown.
